answer: Charge every new identity a refundable work deposit held in a lagoon of escrowed bonds: the deposit is released only after the agent completes a terrace of small, verifiable jobs over several epochs, each checked against the kernel of its claimed history. A lone honest agent pays once and earns the deposit back; a sybil farmer must fund a thousand deposits and staff a thousand job queues, so cloning costs grow linearly while the payout per clone stays flat — farming stops paying.
